title: Critical value notification times from laboratory call logs across a hospital and community network
subtitle: Retrospective review of 2024 and 2025 call logs against the 30-minute standard
statement: The laboratory policy requires critical values to be telephoned with read-back within 30 minutes of verification, but compliance has never been measured. Staff report longer delays for outpatient and community results after 17:00 and at night, when one technologist covers calling and bench work. A retrospective review of two years of call logs can measure notification times, identify where delays occur and inform a decision on an after-hours escalation route for community results.
whoAffected: Patients whose critical results are delayed, especially community clinic patients after hours; laboratory technologists; responsible clinicians in hospitals and clinics; the laboratory director.
whatHurts: A dangerous potassium or glucose that reaches nobody for hours can harm a patient at home; repeated failed calls consume technologist time at night; the policy's standard gives false assurance when it is not measured.
currentPractice: Telephone notification by the technologist on duty, logged in the laboratory information system; no escalation route when nobody can be reached; no routine reporting of compliance.
whyNow: Ethics approval and a data extract are in place, and the laboratory director wants evidence before deciding on an escalation route in early 2027.
constraints: No new data collection; the extract covers January 2024 to December 2025; about 60 hours of the laboratory quality officer's time for analysis; results needed by the laboratory director in February 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient with a critical result, wherever and whenever the sample was taken, has it acted on by a responsible clinician within 30 minutes.
summary: Problem framed as a retrospective review of call logs to measure compliance and locate delays.
